narrative:
The model estimates an 80% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability reflects patterns the system sees in your overall profile compared to others who tend to stay.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this prediction were your access to other job opportunities, your total years of experience across all roles, and the sector you work in. Having received other job offers while at your current company was the strongest driver pushing the prediction toward leaving. Employees who get external offers are far more likely to depart, and your situation matches that pattern exactly. Your 6–10 years of overall experience was the second-biggest factor; while many who stay have only 1–5 years, your longer track record actually increases the model’s expectation that you may move on to new challenges. Finally, working in the “other” sector (rather than medical or education, where most stayers are concentrated) also nudged the prediction toward leaving, though less strongly.

Taken together, these elements created a clear signal that you are likely to leave. The organization should discuss retention measures with you, such as clearer promotion paths or addressing any unmet needs. You may want to reflect on whether your external opportunities or desire for new experiences outweigh staying. Understanding these drivers can help both sides explore practical next steps. (248 words)
